item.title: 🟠 Lessons from 59 Linux Kernel Bug Reports
item.description:
Why this matters: Could affect sign-ins, MFA, or Conditional Access — watch for authentication issues.

Microsoft FORGE Lab researchers used codename MDASH to investigate Linux kernel vulnerabilities, resulting in 59 upstream bug reports, 33 assigned CVEs, and 38 merged fixes. The research includes eight demonstrated local root privilege-escalation exploits and examines the challenges of turning AI-generated findings into validated vulnerabilities and upstream fixes.

The post Lessons from 59 Linux Kernel Bug Reports appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.



Source: Microsoft Security Blog  |  Severity: Important  |  Age: 2d

item.title: 🟠 CVE-2026-100223 Windows NTFS Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
item.description:
Why this matters: Microsoft-platform change — assess user, identity, messaging, or administration impact.
An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists when reparse points are created by sandboxed processes allowing sandbox escape. An attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability could use the sandbox escape to elevate privileges on an affected system. To exploit the vulnerability, an attacker would first have to log on to the system, and then run a specially crafted application to take control over the affected system. The security update addresses the vulnerability by preventing sandboxed processes from creating reparse points targeting inaccessible files.

Source: Microsoft Security Response Center  |  Severity: Important  |  Age: 3d
